text:
Two guard additions in claude-settings, from banchi. Why now: a probe on 2026-11-03 (banchi-only
project thread, three runs) showed that a project's cloud thread loads the claude-settings
guard but never runs a repo's own .claude/settings.json hooks or deny rules. Banchi works
around it by copying its hooks into /etc/claude-code/managed-settings.json in its setup script.
Moving these two into claude-settings makes that copy smaller and serves every repo.

1. TypeScript check after each edit, declared per repo. Model: banchi
   scripts/typecheck-hook.py (PostToolUse on Write|Edit; silent unless the file is .ts/.tsx
   under the declared folder; runs tsc --noEmit there; exit 2 with tsc output on failure;
   fails open on its own bugs). Read the repo's command and folder from
   .claude/layout-extras.json. One home, no per-repo copies. Candidate repos: banchi, q_max,
   joyous, mailaudit.

2. Protected paths, declared per repo. Banchi denies writes to fixtures/ (real TCGplayer
   exports, ground truth for the round-trip test) through a permissions.deny rule and a
   PreToolUse hook. Neither runs in a thread. Add a guard rule that reads a protected-path
   list from .claude/layout-extras.json and denies Write/Edit and shell writes under it.

Both follow building-guard-needs-incident: record the thread gap as the incident, with the
probe date. Each new rule needs its red test first. Port call for other repos: yes, through
layout-extras, opt-in per repo.
